title: universe-cut champion serving pointer + apply-audit record (v4)
description: FROZEN contract for the universe-cut slot's SERVING POINTER. ONE document shape written to THREE keys by crucible-research/scoring/cut_promotion.py::run_cut_promotion on EVERY weekly evaluation, whatever the outcome: config/scanner_cut_champion.json (the live pointer, read by scoring/universe_membership.py::live_cut_champion / resolve_feed_cut), config/apply_audit/scanner_cut_champion/{date}.json (immutable, dated) and config/apply_audit/scanner_cut_champion/latest.json (its mirror). SINCE v4 (alpha-engine-config-I9317) THIS IS NOT WHERE THE DECISION IS TAKEN. The decision is taken by nousergon_lib.arena.engine.run_cycle -- the fleet's single implementation of champion-challenger-policy.md sections 3-6 -- and its full record, with every ladder rung, every pairwise verdict and the confidence-sequence bound behind the pointer, is the arena_cycle artifact at arena/universe_cut/{date}.json. This document transcribes that decision onto the key the serving path reads, and the `arena` block names the cycle it came from. A pointer that does not name its cycle is a claim with no evidence attached.

schema_version.description: v3 -> v4 on the alpha-engine-config-I9317 arena wiring. NOT additive: the required `hysteresis` and `decision_earliest_on` blocks are GONE because the mechanisms they described are abolished (champion-challenger-policy.md section 5.0 removes minimum-evidence floors fleetwide, section 5.2 removes the promotion margin and the cooldown -- Brian's rulings 2026-08-29). A required `arena` block was added. A v3 reader handed a v4 record would find no `hysteresis` block and read a promotion as though a 0.0002/week margin had been cleared, when no margin was applied at all. v2 -> v3 on I9272/I9284; v1 -> v2 on the I8261 cutover.

generated_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 write time. Distinct from decided_on: a re-run on the same trading day rewrites the same dated key with a later generated_at.

decided_on.description: Trading-day-normalised scanner run date — matches the dated audit key and the cuts leaderboard consulted for the vetoes.

decision.description: promote = the pointer moved this evaluation (champion != champion_before). hold = it did not, for the reason in reason_code. A hold is an OUTCOME and is always written; it is never expressed as the absence of a record.

champion.description: The cut the sector-team feed resolves from until the next evaluation. MUST be a member of scoring/universe_membership.py::PROMOTABLE_CUTS — live_cut_champion() raises on anything else rather than serving the default, because a promotion engine that believes one arm is live while the funnel serves another is the 2026-07-22 drift (alpha-engine-config-I7808). NOT an enum since v4: the enum was a hand-maintained literal of two arm names, and the slot has carried five promotable arms since Brian's ruling 2026-08-29 (alpha-engine-config-I9272) -- a promotion to any of the other three would have failed its own contract. The closed set is enforced where it is DERIVED, in universe_membership.live_cut_champion, which raises on a pointer naming anything outside PROMOTABLE_CUTS. A registry restated as a literal in a second file is the drift class this repo has now paid for four times.

champion_before.description: The validated champion read at the start of this evaluation, or DEFAULT_CUT_CHAMPION (attractiveness_top_60) when no pointer had ever been written. Equal to champion on every hold. It is also the leg every arm's paired weekly difference is taken against, which is why a record is not interpretable without it. NOT an enum since v4: the enum was a hand-maintained literal of two arm names, and the slot has carried five promotable arms since Brian's ruling 2026-08-29 (alpha-engine-config-I9272) -- a promotion to any of the other three would have failed its own contract. The closed set is enforced where it is DERIVED, in universe_membership.live_cut_champion, which raises on a pointer naming anything outside PROMOTABLE_CUTS. A registry restated as a literal in a second file is the drift class this repo has now paid for four times.

reason.description: Prose, for the human reconstructing the decision from this artifact alone (principles.md §2.1). Names the metric, the observation count, the shortfall, and what holds.

reason_code.description: Machine-readable outcome, a TRANSCRIPTION of the arena engine's own pointer status (nousergon_lib.arena.engine.PointerDecision.status) plus the one condition that precedes a cycle. 'promoted' is the only value permitted alongside decision='promote' except 'arena_bootstrap', which moves the pointer on a slot that had no eligible incumbent to hold (section 9.1). 'weekly_ledger_missing' means the ledger object does not exist -- an absent store, distinct from a slot that produced no comparison. 'arena_unmeasurable' means no challenger shares a usable window with the incumbent; it ALARMS (section 11: unmeasurable is a first-class status carrying a reason, not a quiet hold). 'arena_unservable' means no arm passed its section 5.3 serving preconditions and is a hard failure of the slot. RETIRED at v4 and never to be re-minted for another condition: insufficient_weeks (the section 5.0-abolished evidence floor), margin_not_met and cooldown_active (the section 5.2-abolished hysteresis), corroborating_horizon_disagrees (a second decision basis on a forward horizon), weekly_ledger_arm_missing (a slot-wide hold on one arm's absence), board_defective (a hold on the corruption of an artifact the decision does not read) and no_promotable_challenger (the 2026-08-21/28 defect itself, now structurally unreachable).

decision_metric.description: The per-date score every arm is graded on: net-of-cost weekly log return MINUS the equal-weight return of the population the arm selected from. Population-relative, never SPY-relative: grading a selection stage against a market index inverted wins and losses on 2026-08-17 when SPY trailed the drawn-from population by 140bp at 21d, and ArenaConfig refuses a selection-stage slot configured against SPY. The pairing against another arm is the engine's job and is deliberately NOT in the name -- every pair is differenced on its OWN longest common window (champion-challenger-policy.md section 4).

decision_cadence.description: One observation per holding period, and the holding period is one weekly re-cut. Successive observations ABUT rather than overlap, which is what makes leaderboard_scoring.date_clustered_stats's 'each date = one independent cluster' contract true here in fact rather than by assumption — and what makes champion-challenger-policy.md §5.1's PSR/DSR/PBO battery computable at all, since those are statistics of a return series.

decision_source.description: The append-only weekly ledger (crucible-research/scoring/weekly_ledger.py), and the ONLY evidence the decision reads. Pinned at import in cut_promotion.py. This constant is one of the three invariants that replaced v1's forbidden_horizons_days: no forward-window horizon can be the decision basis because no leaderboard is.

decision_column.description: The ledger column the score's first term is read from (default net_log_return). Asserted at import against weekly_ledger.LEDGER_COLS. See score_definition for the full arithmetic.

last_promoted_on.description: decided_on of the most recent promote decision, carried forward across holds. Null until the first promotion. The §5.2 cooldown is measured from it.

leaderboard_key.description: The research/cuts_leaderboard/{date}.json the VETOES were evaluated from, so the corroborating numbers can be joined back to their source. Null when no board was available — which under v2 is not a hold: it makes every veto unmeasured and therefore non-blocking (§5.1).

arms.description: Every arm the weekly ledger SCORES, always -- including on a hold, including an arm that produced nothing, and including a retired arm inside its trailing scoring window. Every number here is READ OFF the arena cycle at arena.cycle_key: the ladder for the arm's own record, the incumbent comparison for its head-to-head with its confidence-sequence bound, the pairwise ranking for its standing. None of it is recomputed -- a second implementation of sections 3-6 on the pointer is the drift champion-challenger-policy.md section 10 forbids. Which arms appear is a function of scored_arms on the record, not of this schema file.

n_weeks_scored.description: Weeks that became population-relative scores on this arm's ladder. Reconciled against the cited ledger after the record is written; a disagreement raises CutPromotionError.

n_weeks_paired.description: Paired weeks on the longest common window shared with the incumbent -- read off the arena cycle, never recomputed here.

confseq_supported.description: True only when the whole anytime-valid interval sits above zero -- the promotion signal under section 5.0.

corroborating.description: What the long forward horizons (126d, 252d) said. REPORTED ONLY since v4 and consulted by nothing. They held a veto under the pre-arena engine; the `blocking` / `blocked_by` fields are retained so an archived record stays comparable with its predecessors, and no code path reads them. A forward-window horizon measures a hold the weekly re-cut guarantees never happens, its 'mature' test is a minimum-cohort count of the kind section 5.0 abolishes, and section 4.1 admits one decision basis per slot.

defect.description: Set when an input could not be honestly interpreted -- today, a cuts leaderboard reporting duplicate arm rows. Since v4 a defect does NOT change the pointer decision: the board feeds no part of it, and holding a decision on the corruption of an artifact that does not inform it would be a gate with no mechanism behind it. The record is written, then run_cut_promotion RAISES CutPromotionError -- record first, then fail.

excluded_horizons.description: Per PROMOTABLE arm, what the horizons that are neither a decision input nor a reported corroboration measured, and why they are excluded. Today: 21d, carrying the pre-repair-fundamentals contamination caveat WITH the number so a reader cannot mistake it for a clean read.

ledger.description: Provenance of the per-date score evidence. present:false means the ledger object does not exist on S3 -- absence, never an empty-but-healthy series (champion-challenger-policy.md section 7.2). `per_arm` carries, for every scored arm, how many ledger rows were seen, how many became scores, and the three reasons a row did not: a stale ledger_version, a null decision or population column (an uncomputable transaction cost -- the ledger's whole first week is of this kind), and a row priced over a different span from the rest of the slot that week. Three counters and not one, because they have three different fixes.

excluded_arms.description: Scored arms that may NOT hold the feed, arm -> {arm, reason, scored}. Present on EVERY record, EMPTY under Brian's ruling 2026-08-29 -- a reader must be able to tell "no arm is excluded" from "this record does not say". Before alpha-engine-config-I9272 non-promotability was expressible only as an absence from PROMOTABLE_CUTS, which no artifact could report and no reader could distinguish from an oversight.

scored_arms.description: SLOT_ARMS -- every arm the weekly ledger scores. Derived in universe_membership from the prefixes the cut builder emits at the feed width, so a scored-but-unregistered arm cannot recur.

promotable_arms.description: PROMOTABLE_CUTS -- scored_arms minus the keys of excluded_arms. Recorded so the eligible set on the day of the decision is reconstructable from the artifact alone (principles.md section 2.1).

score_definition.description: The arithmetic that turns ledger columns into the per-date score, e.g. 'net_log_return - population_log_return'. Carried on the record so a reader never has to open the producer to learn what a ladder rung is denominated in.

arena.description: WHERE the decision was actually taken and under what parameters. Required, not optional: this document is deliberately the smaller of the two artifacts now, and a pointer that does not name the cycle it was transcribed from cannot be reconciled against it. `config` carries the ArenaConfig the cycle ran under -- alpha, diff_clip, cap, grace_weeks, min_active_arms, retired_trailing_cycles, retire_evidence -- which champion-challenger-policy.md section 10 requires every slot to name in its registry. `cycle_key` is the authoritative arena_cycle artifact; `retirements` is every verdict INCLUDING the non-retirements and their reasons, because a retirement list containing only retirements cannot be audited (section 6.1).
